solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Minus the trimmings, SW treats served in a shoe? We'll provide the ticket

indicators.note: the trimmed treats are served up inside the shoe, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: DM is short for a Doc Marten, a type of boot or shoe

indicators.note: the outer letters of the treats are trimmed off, leaving only the inside of the word

parts.note: cream teas are the classic treat of south-west England (Devon and Cornwall)

explanation.surface: Someone serving Devon cream teas in a shoe offers a ticket to an event.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea (scones, jam and clotted cream) is the famous treat of England's south-west. A dream ticket is an ideal pair of running mates, here a married couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream ticket is an ideal pairing of candidates, and a dream team is the group that provides one.

clue.text: Make new columns for numbers on bill

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a tab is a bill run up at a bar or restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone adds columns to a bill to break down the figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To tab is to set text in columns with tab stops, so redoing that layout for figures is to tabulate afresh.

clue.text: Lord Bradman, perhaps, second-to-none

parts.note: Sir Don Bradman, the great Australian batsman, is an example of a Don, so a Don
A1 (written AI) means first-rate, second to none

explanation.surface: Praise of the cricketer Don Bradman as an unrivalled lord of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman was Australia's legendary cricket batsman, so 'Bradman, perhaps' is a Don.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonai is a Hebrew name for God used in Jewish worship, meaning my Lord.

clue.text: Taste something spicy? Not Romeo — nor I, his rival

indicators.note: not Romeo says the letter standing for Romeo is left out of the phrase

parts.note: to try something is to taste it
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: nor carries the earlier not forward to a second letter, which leaves the curry dish

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry dish

explanation.surface: An invitation to try a curry, apparently turned down by Romeo and a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY BALTI loses R ('Not Romeo') and then I ('nor I'). 'his' points back to Romeo, so the definition is Romeo's rival.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, Tybalt is Juliet's hot-headed cousin, the enemy who fights Romeo and is killed by him.

clue.text: A material from space

parts.note: material in the sense of physical or tangible means real

explanation.surface: A substance arriving from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' is not outer space but space in the sense of area.
explanation.definitionFit: Areal is the adjective of area, describing something relating to a surface or region, hence measured from space in that sense.

clue.text: I yield: her 50.1% tops my 49.9%

parts.note: a husband conceding that his wife makes up slightly more than half of the couple, and the superior half at that

explanation.surface: A husband concedes that his wife's share of the partnership just outweighs his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Like several entries, this is a nickname for a wife: the figures say she is the bigger, better of two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The better half is a jokey term for one's spouse, usually a wife, implying she is the superior partner.

clue.text: Toast 'Ten!' and 'Tin!' with a cruise for richer/poorer or sickness/health?

indicators.note: something that is toast is wrecked, so these words are smashed up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Wedding anniversary toasts, tin and ten years, and a celebratory cruise, set against the marriage vows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' signals the anagram of TEN, TIN and A CRUISE. Tin is the gift for a tenth wedding anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: The marriage vows' pairs of richer or poorer and sickness or health are the unknowns a couple promises to face together.

clue.text: I doubt her fan letters bothered 25 26a!

indicators.note: letters that are bothered are disturbed and stirred around into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband doubts the woman who keeps getting fan mail, and the letters bother him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 25/26 (ME OLD DUTCH), another name for a wife. The answer is Cockney rhyming slang: trouble and strife rhymes with wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are Cockney slang for one's wife, so one stands for the other as a synonym.

clue.text: 'I avoid her' — Arthur, so saying, means to enter Ireland?

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
doors are the means by which one enters a building

explanation.surface: A man dodging his wife says he will slip off to Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Daley, the wheeler-dealer in the British TV series Minder, called his never-seen wife 'er indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Daley's phrase for the wife he keeps away from has become a stock jokey term for one's wife.

clue.text: In the revamped BTec, introductions to entrance exam oddly inverted

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters go within the word the
revamped means redone and reorganised, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written; a BTEC is a British vocational qualification

indicators.note: introductions are the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A student finds an exam paper on a revised BTec course printed upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The BTec is a British vocational qualification. 'In' looks like a link word but is the container signal, and 'oddly inverted' is the definition, not a reversal instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tête-bêche describes a pair of stamps printed with one upside down relative to the other, so oddly inverted.

clue.text: In one type of music, you must have the heart to debar plucked instrument

indicators.note: in places the heart of the word inside the music abbreviation

parts.note: R&B, rhythm and blues, is a music genre, written RB

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here everything but the ends

explanation.surface: Advice that a certain kind of music needs heart to keep a performer away.
explanation.walkthrough: R&B is rhythm and blues; the ampersand is dropped in the grid letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebab is a bowed or plucked stringed instrument of North Africa and the Middle East.

clue.text: Manufacture pork pies for one entering river port

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the word for telling untruths

parts.note: pork pies is rhyming slang for lies, so to manufacture them is to lie
eg (for example) is the usual signal for an example, 'for one'

explanation.surface: A factory makes pork pies for one customer coming into a port.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pies (porkies) are lies in Cockney rhyming slang; 'Manufacture' turns the noun into the verb to lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a Belgian city on the river Meuse, with one of Europe's biggest inland ports.

clue.text: What we said to detectives in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so this pair of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: to in the sense of at, as in face to face, near or at
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: Someone recalls what they told the detectives during a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we' is the royal or editorial we: a dictum is a pronouncement, so dicta are things we said.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicta, plural of dictum, are pronouncements or sayings, things an authority has said.

clue.text: Couples fired up by Christmas Day dalliance

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
by means the answer sits beside and within these words, held by them

explanation.surface: Couples get excited by a flirtation over Christmas Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' picks SDAYD out of Christmas Day dalliance and 'fired up' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyad is a pair, two things or people considered as a unit.

clue.text: A chap's rib with Row 5's middle C — I've got it in range

parts.note: ha, short for aha, is the exclamation of sudden understanding

explanation.surface: A man boasts of having caught something with a rib and a middle C.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A chap's rib with Row 5's middle' is a second indication: joined to the middle four letters of row 5 in the grid, the answer gives a biblical phrase for Adam's rib, that is, Eve, a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains is a mountain range, so chain is a synonym for range.

clue.text: Make play for Clio?

definitions.meaning: to entertain them, make them play or enjoy themselves
Clio is one of the nine Muses, so an example of a muse

explanation.surface: A command to make a play for the Muse of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is the Muse of history, one of nine goddesses, and amusing someone means entertaining them.

clue.text: Tell someone's alter ego from yours at first sight

parts.note: to someone, an alter ego is 'not I', another self

indicators.note: the first letters seen are the opening letters of the two words before

explanation.surface: Telling a person their other self apart from yours at a glance.
explanation.walkthrough: An alter ego is literally another I, so from the speaker's point of view it is NOT I.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify someone is to inform them, a synonym for tell.

clue.text: See 23
Pacific atoll that a fun-run takes in

indicators.note: the phrase takes the answer inside it, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A charity fun run passes through a Pacific atoll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' hides ATAFU inside 'that a fun'.
explanation.definitionFit: Atafu is a coral atoll in Tokelau, a New Zealand territory in the South Pacific.

clue.text: See 23
See 8
Use it to apprehend fences of narcotics?

definitions.text: Use it to apprehend fences of narcotics?

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize, so one piece takes the other into custody inside it

parts.note: the answer used as a verb

indicators.note: the fences of a word are its outer letters, the first and last enclosing the rest

explanation.surface: Advice to trust your instincts when catching those who handle stolen drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a sense is what you use to apprehend things. Read again, one way to sense, SEE, 'to apprehend' holds NS, the 'fences of' narcotics. A fence is also a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense such as sight is a faculty you use to perceive, which is one meaning of apprehend.

clue.text: I'm sorry to admit a mistake so marked beer's put out

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: eh? is what you say for I'm sorry, what did you say?
a cross, X, is how a mistake is marked
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: An apology for a mistake that marked a beer as out of stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm sorry' here is the request to repeat, eh?, not an apology; 'to admit' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, putting air out of the lungs.

clue.text: 'I serve her', says the man at the bar?

definitions.text: 'I serve her', says the man at the bar?

parts.words: 'I serve her', says the man at the bar?
parts.note: a barrister, a man called to the bar, describing the wife he serves and obeys

explanation.surface: A barman says he is serving a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The man at the bar is not a barman but a barrister: Horace Rumpole, in John Mortimer's Rumpole of the Bailey stories, calls his formidable wife by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpole's name for his domineering wife, borrowed from H. Rider Haggard's novel She, is a jokey term for any commanding wife.

clue.text: Islamic man I see cutting border

indicators.note: the exclamation cuts into the border word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border
ah is said when you suddenly see, or understand

explanation.surface: A Muslim man appears as someone understands what is crossing a border.
explanation.definitionFit: Rahim is a Muslim man's name, from the Arabic for merciful, one of the names of God.

clue.text: 'I adore her' in Bow (versatile model from Amsterdam?)

indicators.note: versatile means turning readily from one thing to another, so the letters turn into a new order

parts.note: something from Amsterdam is Dutch; the question mark says Amsterdam is just one Dutch city

explanation.surface: A man adores a versatile Dutch model he met in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London; being born within the sound of Bow Bells makes you a Cockney, so 'in Bow' means in Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Me old Dutch is Cockney slang for one's wife, from the music-hall song My Old Dutch.

clue.text: See 25
Squeezes fruit under palm?

definitions.meaning: squeezes is slang for girlfriends or boyfriends
... grow in clusters hanging beneath the fronds of the date palm

explanation.surface: Pressing the fruit gathered from under a palm tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeeze is a sweetheart, someone you go out with, and dates grow on date palms.

clue.text: Stopping short of glycerides and salt, change excitedly

indicators.note: stopping as in filling a gap, so these pieces plug the middle of the word for change

parts.note: to alter something is to change it
fats are glycerides, so a food short of them is low-fat, spelt LO-FAT on labels
salt in the sense of dry humour is wit

explanation.surface: Cutting back on fats and salt, someone changes their diet in excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Fats are chemically glycerides, so food short of them is low-fat, spelt LO-FAT on labels. Attic salt is an old term for refined wit.
explanation.definitionFit: All of a twitter is an idiom for being agitated or in a state of nervous excitement.

clue.text: A burst of hot air to disable works

indicators.note: works as a verb, kneads or reshapes, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A sudden blast of heat that can put machinery out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle boast is empty bragging, and hot air is slang for empty talk.
